newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary may let western energy investors pull out.
newsitem.headline: Hungary may let western energy investors pull out.

text.p: Belgian utility Tractebel and other western investors, which bought stakes in Hungary's electricity companies one year ago, may get a chance to pull out following a government decision on Thursday.

Government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference that the government would allow the investors to sell their stakes with the special permission of the privatisation and industry ministers earlier than the agreed five years after the sale.
"The idea arose that it would be reasonable to draw in new investors in certain areas," he said.
He said he did not know which investor wanted to sell its shares.

Tractebel was reported earlier this month to be looking to sell back its 48.7 percent stake in the Hungarian power station Dunamenti after the Hungarian government announced January energy price rises below its expectations.
The Belgians are believed to be unhappy about the government's decision to allow utilities to increase retail electricity prices by 24.9 percent from January, a hike which was postpgned from October.

Tractebel was one of a number of West European utilities, including RWE and Electricite de France, which paid a total of around $2 billion at the end of last year for stakes in Hungary's energy sector in the biggest utility sell- off of any post-Communist state.
